title: How many passwords can a five digit lock have?
description: {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} find an old safe with a five digit lock. The video starts with a two digit lock and grows it one slot at a time, and Keeko doubts what ten to the power five means.
teaching_notes: One idea: each new slot multiplies the number of passwords by ten, so a simpler lock shows the pattern. Watch for students who read ten to the power five as five times ten.

source: How many passwords does a 2-digit, a 3-digit and a 5-digit lock have?
video_script.why: A learner sees that every extra digit slot multiplies the passwords by ten, and how ten to the power five is built.
video_script.substitution: the book's own safe and its simpler two digit and three digit locks
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} at the old safe with the digit lock
video_script.wrong_move: reads ten to the power five as five times ten
video_script.payoff_line: A five digit lock has one lakh passwords

final_answer.spoken: one hundred, one thousand and one lakh passwords

names.{{NAME_1}}: finds the old safe with the five digit lock
names.{{NAME_2}}: finds the old safe with the five digit lock

maths_rules: 10^5 is five tens multiplied, not 5 x 10 = 50
video_script.design: One idea: each extra slot multiplies by ten. Wrong idea: ten to the power five is five times ten. The lock grows from two slots to five and the total only appears at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the old safe with five digit slots; {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} beside it

marks.safe: the old safe with its five digit slots appears, {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} beside it
marks.try: the slots turn through the digits one password after another
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the lock

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='safe'/>{{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} find an old safe with stamps and coins. It has a five digit lock.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Nobody knows the password, so they try every password until it opens.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many passwords might they have to try?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a lock with one slot and the digits 0 to 9; the line: if a problem is hard, try a simpler version

marks.simple: the words try a simpler version appear
marks.slot: one slot of the lock turns through the digits 0 to 9
marks.ten: ten choices are counted along the digits

narration: <bookmark mark='simple'/>When a problem is too big, try a simpler version of it first.
<bookmark mark='slot'/>A lock with two slots is simpler than one with five.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Each slot can show any digit from zero to nine, so each slot has ten choices.

beats.on_screen: Given: 5 slots, each with the digits 0 to 9

marks.given: five slots are drawn, each marked with the digits 0 to 9

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a lock with five slots, and each slot has ten digits to choose from.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of passwords

marks.find: the words number of passwords are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many passwords the lock can have.

beats.on_screen: two slots: 10 choices for the first slot, 10 for the second under each; 10 x 10 = 100

marks.first: the first slot shows ten branches
marks.second: each branch grows ten more for the second slot

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, take two slots. The first slot has ten choices.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Under each choice, the second slot also has ten choices.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Ten times ten gives one hundred passwords, from zero zero to nine nine.

beats.on_screen: a third slot added; 100 x 10 = 1000; a fourth slot: 1000 x 10 = 10000

marks.third: a third slot is added to every one of the 100 passwords
marks.four: 1000 x 10 = 10000 appears for a fourth slot

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step two, add a third slot. Each of the hundred passwords takes ten choices for it.
<bookmark mark='three'/>One hundred times ten gives one thousand passwords.
<bookmark mark='four'/>A fourth slot multiplies by ten again, which gives ten thousand.

beats.on_screen: a fifth slot: 10000 x 10; the line 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 with five tens

marks.five: a fifth slot is added and 10000 x 10 is written
marks.tens: 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 appears with the five tens counted

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, add the fifth slot. That is ten thousand times ten.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Every slot brought one ten, so five slots are five tens multiplied together. We write that as ten to the power five.

marks.ans: the three answers are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>A five digit lock has one lakh passwords.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>A two digit lock has one hundred, and a three digit lock has one thousand.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 10 to the power 5 = 5 x 10 = 50, struck out; 10 x 10 = 100 beside it

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows 10 to the power 5 = 5 x 10 = 50
marks.fix: 10 x 10 = 100 for the two digit lock appears beside the bubble
marks.all: the bubble is struck out and five tens are written multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a five digit lock has fifty passwords. Ten to the power five, says Keeko, is five times ten.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a two digit lock already has ten times ten, which is one hundred. Fifty is too small.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The power tells us how many tens are multiplied, not how many times we add ten.
